subtopics.title: Site, Situation and the Rural World

questions.question: The difference between site and situation is that:
options: Site is the settlement's position relative to its surroundings; situation is the land it stands on
Site is the actual land a settlement stands on; situation is its position relative to rivers, routes and other places
Site applies only to cities and situation only to villages
They mean the same thing on a topographic map

questions.question: A rural settlement with houses clustered around a shared borehole is classified by pattern as:
Which is a PUSH factor driving rural-urban migration?
The land reform leg that returns land to people dispossessed after 1913 is called:

subtopics.title: Urban Settlements — Hierarchy, Structure and Issues

questions.question: Urbanisation is best defined as:
options: The outward spread of a city's built-up area
An increasing percentage of a population living in urban areas
The growth of informal settlements only
People moving from big cities to small towns

questions.question: A specialist heart hospital is a high-order service because it:
options: Has a small sphere of influence
Needs a very large threshold population and has a large range

questions.question: In the South African city model, townships and informal settlements typically lie:
options: On the far periphery, separated from the core by old buffer zones

questions.question: Urban blight is most closely associated with which zone?
options: The transition zone of decaying older buildings around the CBD

subtopics.title: Economic Geography — Sectors, Farms, Mines and Factories

questions.question: Sorting activities into sectors: fishing, car assembly, banking and university research are respectively:
Agriculture contributes only a few percent of South Africa's GDP, yet it is considered vital because:
options: It anchors food security, exports and rural employment
It is the largest sector by GDP

questions.question: Which list names the four core industrial regions as a set?
options: Gauteng (PWV), Durban-Pinetown, Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage, South-western Cape
Coega, Saldanha, Richards Bay, East London

questions.question: The difference between an IDZ and an SDI is that:
options: An IDZ is a farming scheme; an SDI is a mine
An IDZ is inland only; an SDI is at ports only
They are two names for the same policy
An IDZ is a purpose-built industrial estate linked to a port; an SDI is a development corridor linking regions

subtopics.title: The Section B Toolkit — Calculations, Interpretation and GIS

questions.question: On a 1:50 000 topographic map, one centimetre represents:
Average gradient is calculated as:
options: Horizontal equivalent divided by vertical interval
Vertical interval divided by horizontal equivalent, expressed as a ratio like 1:20
Vertical scale divided by horizontal scale

questions.question: Compared to the 1:50 000 topographic map, the 1:10 000 orthophoto map is:
options: Five times larger in scale, showing photographic detail with contours
The same scale but in colour

questions.question: In GIS, drawing a zone of stated width around a river to see which features fall inside it is called:

subtopics.title: The Village, the Taxi and the City

questions.question: In the story, the village shop closes after many residents leave because the shop lost its:
options: Threshold population — the minimum customers it needs to survive

questions.question: The old strips of open ground separating the township from the rest of the city in the South African model are called:
options: Buffer zones drawn by apartheid planners

questions.question: Sipho's long daily commute from the periphery to work near the core illustrates:
options: The high accessibility of the CBD
How the apartheid city model placed homes far from workplaces

subtopics.title: How the Country Earns Its Keep

questions.question: In the household picture, the grandmother who grows and digs stands for:
options: The primary sector — agriculture, fishing and mining

questions.question: The 'extension cord run to a neighbour's harbour' describes:
options: An Industrial Development Zone like Coega
A Spatial Development Initiative corridor like the Maputo Corridor

questions.question: The street vendor at the taxi rank and the backyard salon belong to:
options: The informal sector — unregistered, small-scale, but a vital survival net

questions.question: A gradient answer of 1:20 means:
options: You climb twenty metres for every one metre walked
You climb one metre for every twenty metres of horizontal distance
The map is twenty times exaggerated

questions.question: Vertical exaggeration is calculated as:
options: Vertical scale divided by horizontal scale, answered as so-many times
Vertical interval divided by horizontal equivalent
Map distance times the scale denominator

questions.question: Why does an answer of '4' for a distance calculation lose a mark even if the number is right?
options: Because distance answers must be in centimetres only
Because the unit of measurement must be given in the final answer
Because distances must be whole numbers

questions.question: The evidence habit for map interpretation means:
options: Backing every claim with visible map evidence, like windpumps and cultivated land proving a rural settlement
Always choosing the first option in multiple choice
